# Primitives

54 primitives, each compiled through both backends to produce this page.

Two halves per row, and neither is written here. The **intent** below is the doc comment
above the variant in `hozo_ir`'s `Primitive` enum, which is where a primitive's purpose is
recorded and the one place that cannot drift from the set. The **Web** and **React Native**
columns are what the compiler emitted for a snippet, in the same run that wrote this file.

## Where the role has to be said out loud

A different tag name is not a difference worth printing: a `<section>` and a `View` are the
same box. What is worth knowing is where a role has to be *written* on one side and not the
other, because that is the work the compiler is doing.

Both columns are the role written into the output. On the Web most of these are blank
because the element already carries the role -- a `<nav>` is a navigation landmark without
anybody saying so -- while React Native has no elements, so every role it keeps is one the
compiler put there. A blank on the React Native side is a role that platform has no word
for, and those are the ones that are genuinely lost.

## What each one is for

**`ActivityIndicator`** — A busy indicator: `HozoActivityIndicator` on Web, which draws its own spinner, and React Native's `ActivityIndicator`. The Web half exists because there is no element for this and a project should not have to bring one.

**`Address`** — Contact/address semantics: `<address>` on Web and `View` on React Native.

**`AnimatedView`** — React Native Animated's namespace View component.

**`Article`** — A self-contained document composition: `<article>` on Web and a role-bearing `View` on React Native.

**`Aside`** — A complementary region/sidebar: `<aside>` on Web and `role="complementary"` `View` on React Native.

**`Button`** — A control that submits an intent: `<button>` on Web and a `Pressable` carrying `accessibilityRole="button"` on React Native. Not React Native's own `Button`, which takes a `title` and renders no children -- see `INCOMPATIBLE_PRIMITIVES`.

**`Code`** — Inline code literal: `<code>` on Web and monospace `Text` on React Native.

**`Description`** — A description/value within a term list: `<dd>` on Web and `View` on React Native.

**`Details`** — A disclosure widget container: `<details>` on Web and collapsible `View` on React Native.

**`Dialog`** — A modal dialog (proposal §10.3, v1's first hard primitive). A primitive rather than a component the compiler walks past, because otherwise its `className` never compiles and its missing accessible name is never noticed -- both backends lower it to `/behaviors`'s `Dialog`, which owns the runtime behaviour.

**`Emphasis`** — Stress emphasis: `<em>` on Web and `Text` with italic font style on React Native.

**`Fieldset`** — A form control grouping container: `<fieldset>` on Web and `role="group"` `View` on React Native.

**`Figcaption`** — A figure caption: `<figcaption>` on Web and `Text` on React Native.

**`Figure`** — A figure container: `<figure>` on Web and `role="figure"` `View` on React Native.

**`FlatList`** — A data-driven list. Web keeps the lightweight core renderer while Native lowers to React Native's virtualized FlatList.

**`Footer`** — A landmark footer/contentinfo: `<footer>` on Web and `role="contentinfo"` `View` on React Native.

**`Header`** — A landmark header/banner: `<header>` on Web and `role="banner"` `View` on React Native.

**`Heading`** — A document heading: `<h1>`...`<h6>` on Web and an accessible header `Text` on React Native.

**`Image`** — An image with a universal string `src`: `<img src>` on Web and React Native's `<Image source={{ uri }}>` on Native.

**`Legend`** — A caption/label for a fieldset: `<legend>` on Web and bold `Text` on React Native.

**`Link`** — A destination-bearing interaction: `<a>` on Web and Hozo's `Linking.openURL` wrapper on React Native.

**`List`** — A static semantic list: `<ul>`/`<ol>` on Web and a list-role `View` on React Native. Data-heavy lists remain `FlatList`.

**`ListItem`** — One static list entry: `<li>` on Web and a listitem-role `View` on React Native.

**`Main`** — The primary content landmark: `<main>` on Web and `role="main"` `View` on React Native.

**`Mark`** — Highlighted/marked text: `<mark>` on Web and highlighted `Text` on React Native.

**`Modal`** — React Native's top-layer presentation surface.

**`Nav`** — A navigation landmark: `<nav>` on Web and a role-bearing `View` on React Native.

**`NoBreak`** — Non-breaking inline container: `<span style="white-space: nowrap">` on Web and non-breaking space replacement on React Native.

**`Paragraph`** — A block of prose: `<p>` on Web and `Text` on React Native.

**`Pressable`** — A surface that responds to a press: `<div>` with the keyboard handlers a `<button>` gets for free on Web, and `Pressable` on React Native. Carries no role of its own, which is why writing one is the commonest thing `A11Y_INTERACTIVE_WITHOUT_ROLE` asks for.

**`Progress`** — A progress indicator bar: `<progress>` on Web and `role="progressbar"` `View` on React Native.

**`RefreshControl`** — Pull-to-refresh intent nested in a ScrollView or FlatList.

**`Ruby`** — CJK ruby annotation container: `<ruby>` on Web and ruby layout with duplicate-speech suppression on React Native.

**`RubyText`** — CJK ruby text annotation: `<rt>` on Web and furigana text on React Native.

**`ScrollView`** — A viewport that scrolls vertically by default and horizontally when `horizontal` is set. Its content layout stays explicit in children.

**`Search`** — A search landmark container: `<search>` on Web and `role="search"` `View` on React Native.

**`Section`** — A thematic document region: `<section>` on Web and `View` on React Native, where there is no corresponding layout primitive.

**`Separator`** — A thematic break or divider: `<hr>` on Web and `role="separator"` `View` on React Native.

**`Small`** — Side comments and small print: `<small>` on Web and small `Text` on React Native.

**`Strikethrough`** — Strikethrough/deleted text: `<s>` on Web and `Text` with line-through on React Native.

**`Strong`** — Bold/strong importance: `<strong>` on Web and `Text` with bold font weight on React Native.

**`Sub`** — Subscript: `<sub>` on Web and subscripted `Text` on React Native.

**`Summary`** — A disclosure summary/trigger: `<summary>` on Web and `Pressable` on React Native.

**`Sup`** — Superscript: `<sup>` on Web and superscripted `Text` on React Native.

**`Svg`** — An SVG element, by its own name: `Svg`, `Rect`, `Path`, `G`. One variant rather than fourteen because the lowering really is uniform -- Web writes the lowercase tag, React Native imports the capitalised component of the same name from `react-native-svg` -- so a variant each would be fourteen identical match arms in every backend and one more place to forget an element. The name is the SVG one, and the JSX spelling is `<Svg.Rect>`: a namespace rather than a prefix, because `Text` is both an SVG element and a Hozo primitive and `SvgText` would be a name neither the specification nor `react-native-svg` uses.

**`Term`** — A term/name within a term list: `<dt>` on Web and bold `Text` on React Native.

**`TermList`** — A term-and-description list container: `<dl>` on Web and `role="list"` `View` on React Native.

**`Text`** — A run of text: `<span>` on Web and `Text` on React Native. Not a box. It carries no flex base on either platform, so `display: flex` on one means what CSS says it means.

**`TextInput`** — A single-line text field. `<input>` on Web, `TextInput` on React Native -- and the reason `placeholder-*` can lower at all, since React Native carries that colour as a prop on this component rather than as a style on anything.

**`Time`** — A machine-readable date/time representation: `<time>` on Web and `Text` on React Native.

**`TouchableOpacity`** — React Native's opacity-feedback press target. Web lowering keeps the feedback in a tiny runtime component; Native keeps TouchableOpacity.

**`TouchableWithoutFeedback`** — A press target that attaches behavior to its only child instead of introducing a layout box.

**`Underline`** — Underlined text: `<u>` on Web and `Text` with underline text decoration on React Native.

**`View`** — The box everything else is built from: `<div>` on Web and `View` on React Native. A column flex container on both, which is React Native's default and not CSS's -- the Web side carries a base style that says so, and `is_view_box` names every primitive that shares it.
